stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Bartolome de las Casas, A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies (written 1542, published 1552). Las Casas wrote that the peoples of Hispaniola were gentle, obedient, and owned little, and that the Spanish fell upon them like wolves, killing them and forcing them into hard labor. He claimed that the Indigenous population of Hispaniola had fallen from about three million to only two hundred. He sent the account to Prince Philip of Spain to persuade the crown to stop the cruelty.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of a public-domain text; Las Casas, Brevisima relacion (1542, published 1552).

stem: A student wants to use this passage as evidence for the exact size of the Indigenous population of Hispaniola in 1542. What most limits the passage for that use?

options.text: Las Casas wrote the account in Latin, so Spanish officials could not read it.
Las Casas wrote after 1607, so he describes a later century.
Las Casas wrote to persuade the crown, and his population figures are contested.
Las Casas was a Portuguese sailor who never visited the Americas.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
